newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Gehe gets boost from Lloyds Chemists.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Gehe gets boost from Lloyds Chemists.

text.p: German drug wholesaler Gehe AG on Wednesday said its newly-acquired British unit Lloyds Chemists Plc was already well integrated and helped it post a 15.4 percent profit rise in the first half of 1997.

Gehe clinched the deal for Lloyds Chemists in January after a year-long takeover battle with Unichem. The German firm outgunned Unichem with a cash bid of 685 million pounds, securing itself a strong role in British retail pharmacy.
Since then, Gehe said it had made 230 million pounds by selling off non-core operations at Lloyds Chemists, in line with the takeover conditions set by the British government.

Gehe reported pre-tax profit of 226.5 million marks for the first six months of the year on sales of 12.4 billion marks, up 18.3 percent. Discounting Lloyds and a separate drugs unit sell-off, sales would have risen four percent.

Full-year profits would show an increase of 15 to 20 percent, Gehe predicted, repeating an earlier forecast that sales including Lloyds should hit 24.5 billion marks by the end of the year, up from 21.4 billion in 1996.
Lloyds had already been "smoothly" integrated with Gehe's own British unit AAH, Gehe said.
AAH's 322 pharmacies have linked up with Lloyds' 904 outlets to create a new British retail pharmacy division.

Gehe said it had set up a new management team to oversee the newly-merged AAH/Lloyds pharmaceutical wholesale business in Britain and had decided to establish a joint administrative centre in Coventry.
Gehe noted that selling off some Lloyds Chemists operations had both satisfied regulatory conditions and cut the price of buying the company by around a third.
